nodes.summary: Validity of the bound (Hudson–Kaplan 1985): a valid breakpoint set has at least as many points as any family of pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals, since each interval needs its own breakpoint.
nodes.title: Validity of the bound

nodes.summary: No family of pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals has more than `R_m` members.
nodes.title: Greedy optimality

nodes.summary: The right endpoints of the kept intervals are distinct, so there are `R_m` of them.
nodes.title: The sweep yields exactly $R_m$ distinct breakpoints

nodes.summary: The haplotypes carrying allele `a` at site `i`; when `a` is the derived allele this is the clade defined by the mutation at `i`.
nodes.title: Haplotypes carrying an allele at a site

nodes.summary: The bound is attained: some valid breakpoint set has exactly `R_m` points, so `R_m` is the minimum size of a valid breakpoint set.
nodes.title: $R_m$ is the minimum size of a valid breakpoint set

nodes.summary: The sweep attains the maximum: `R_m` is the largest size of a family of pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals.
nodes.title: $R_m$ is the maximum number of disjoint four-gamete intervals

nodes.summary: Sites `i` and `j` show all four gametes: for every pair of alleles `(a, b)` some haplotype carries `a` at `i` and `b` at `j`. This reuses `Cslib.Bioinformatics.Phylogenetics.Splits.FourGametes` applied to the site columns `(M · i)` and `(M · j)`; it is not a second definition of the four-gamete predicate.
nodes.title: Four-gamete condition for two sites

nodes.summary: Cutting immediately to the left of the right endpoint of every kept interval gives a valid breakpoint set.
nodes.title: Sweep cuts form a valid breakpoint set

nodes.summary: A set `B` of breakpoints is valid for the sample `M` when it separates every pair of sites `i < j` showing all four gametes.
nodes.title: Valid set of recombination breakpoints

nodes.summary: The intervals kept by the sweep are pairwise disjoint four-gamete intervals.
nodes.title: Hudson–Kaplan sweep yields disjoint four-gamete intervals

nodes.summary: A family `F` of site pairs `(i, j)` consists of four-gamete intervals (`i < j`, all four gametes at `i` and `j`) that are pairwise disjoint: of two distinct intervals, one ends at or before the start of the other, so no breakpoint separates both.
nodes.title: Disjoint family of four-gamete intervals

nodes.summary: The intervals kept by the sweep are distinct.
nodes.title: Intervals kept by the Hudson–Kaplan sweep are distinct

nodes.summary: Two sites miss one of the four gametes exactly when, for some choice of the alleles `a` at `i` and `b` at `j` (the derived alleles), the carrier sets are nested or disjoint, as two clades of one rooted tree are.
nodes.title: Characterization of site pairs failing the four-gamete test

nodes.summary: `R_m` is a lower bound (Hudson–Kaplan 1985): every valid breakpoint set has at least `R_m` points.
nodes.title: `R_m` is a lower bound

nodes.summary: Suppose the breakpoints `B` cut the sequence into blocks such that, within a block, the derived-allele clades of every two sites are nested or disjoint for some choice of the derived alleles (as for sites whose mutations sit on one tree under the infinite-sites model). Then there are at least `R_m` breakpoints.
nodes.title: Hudson and Kaplan's bound for tree-like blocks

nodes.summary: The number of intervals kept by the sweep.
nodes.title: Hudson and Kaplan's `R_m`

nodes.summary: A breakpoint `g` (a cut immediately to the left of site `g`) separates sites `i` and `j` when `i < g ≤ j`.
nodes.title: Breakpoint separating two sites

nodes.summary: One step of the sweep at right endpoint `j`. The list `acc` holds the intervals kept so far, most recent first; the next interval must start at or after the right end of the most recent one (at or after site `0` if none was kept). Among the admissible four-gamete intervals ending at `j`, the shortest one is kept.
nodes.title: One step of the Hudson–Kaplan sweep

nodes.summary: The intervals kept by Hudson and Kaplan's left-to-right sweep, most recent first.
nodes.title: Hudson–Kaplan left-to-right sweep

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
